title: URLSession with async/await: decoding, and the error state

videos.script: Until now the planner's data was written into the program. Today it comes from a server. {{server}} A small one, seventy lines of Python, running on your own machine. It answers with JSON, and it can answer badly on purpose. {{await}} Asking it something is one line, with await in front. And this whole lesson runs on Linux, because URLSession is part of Swift's open-source Foundation. {{decode}} The answer is bytes. JSONDecoder turns them into Swift values, through a type that speaks the server's spelling. {{status}} Then the part most apps get wrong. A 404 is not an error to URLSession. It is an answer. So the planner gets one client that checks three things, in order. Was there an answer? Was it a success? Is it the shape we expected? {{states}} Every screen that loads something has three states. Loading, loaded, and failed. You make them one type, so none can be forgotten. {{cancel}} And a request nobody is waiting for should stop. You cancel one, you time one out, and you watch the server finish the work anyway.
